Answer: C
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 1a) demonstrates a large right-sided pleural effusion and an air-fluid level within the mediastinum (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of a mediastinal abscess resulting from esophageal perforation by the fishbone. This correlates with the clinical history of hematemesis and circulatory collapse, ruling out simple effusion or isolated pneumomediastinum.
